articles.title: The Plan: Balance and Nuance Reign at Gowanus’ Douglass Port
articles.narrative: Charney Companies and Tavros have completed Douglass Port, a 15-story, 260-unit residential building at 251 Douglass Street in Brooklyn's Gowanus neighborhood. This property is part of the larger Gowanus Wharf campus, a multi-building development offering thousands of mixed-income units. Residents of Douglass Port, which began leasing in June and is currently 20% leased, have access to shared amenities across the entire campus, including a rooftop pool at the Union Channel building and a basketball court at Douglass Port, fostering a strong community environment.

data_points.notable_features: 58 units designated as affordable housing under the 421-a tax program; shared amenities across the Gowanus Wharf campus including a rooftop pool and basketball court; units feature kitchen islands and abundant natural light.
data_points.project_notes: Part of the larger Gowanus Wharf residential campus, which includes several rental buildings with shared amenities.

articles.title: Lefrak Offloads Brooklyn Rent-Stabilized Assets to HF NYC for $38 million
articles.narrative: LeFrak has sold its Parkway Portfolio, comprising four rent-stabilized multifamily properties with over 300 units in Brooklyn's Bensonhurst and Midwood neighborhoods, to HF NYC for $38 million. J.P. Morgan Chase provided a $24.8 million acquisition loan for the purchase. The transaction comes shortly after the New York City Rent Guidelines Board voted to freeze rents on one- and two-year leases in rent-stabilized buildings.

data_points.address: 8301 and 7705 Bay Parkway, Brooklyn, NY; 1201 and 1640 Ocean Parkway, Brooklyn, NY

articles.title: Target Inks 135K-SF Lease at Queens’ Rego Park Shopping Center
articles.narrative: Target has signed a 15-year lease for 135,000 square feet at the Rego Park Shopping Center in Queens, bringing the multi-level, open-air mall to 99 percent occupancy. The retail giant will occupy space in the Rego Park II section of the center, which is anchored by a wholesale retailer and includes a strong mix of other national retailers.

data_points.notable_features: Multi-level, 600,000-square-foot open-air mall anchored by a wholesale giant.

articles.market_intelligence: Recent asking rents for retail space in Queens averaged $42.47 per square foot.

articles.title: Rent Guidelines Board Vote Sends New York’s Landlords Into Uncharted Territory
articles.narrative: The New York City Rent Guidelines Board (RGB) voted 7-1 to freeze rents for one- and two-year leases on rent-stabilized apartments, a decision that has drawn strong criticism from landlord advocacy groups and legal experts. Critics argue that Mayor Zohran Mamdani's recent appointments to the RGB predetermined the outcome, disregarding statutory requirements for data-driven decisions. Landlord representatives contend that without rent increases, property owners cannot afford to maintain rent-stabilized units, and lawsuits are expected to challenge the legality of the freeze. Conversely, proponents of the freeze cite RGB data indicating a 6.2% increase in net operating income for landlords of rent-stabilized units, suggesting owners can absorb the freeze while tenants face significant financial burdens.

articles.title: BridgeCity Lends $72M on Long Island City Apartments Build
articles.narrative: Elmord Management secured $72.3 million in acquisition and construction financing from BridgeCity Capital for a new 161-unit multifamily development in Long Island City, Queens. The project will rise on a former industrial site at 44-68 Vernon Boulevard, which Elmord Management acquired for $28 million. The 16-story building will feature 142,697 square feet of residential and commercial space, transforming a site near a prominent former development proposal.

articles.title: Largo Capital Arranges $17.5M Permanent Loan for Buffalo Industrial Building
articles.narrative: Largo Capital has arranged a $17.5 million permanent loan for a 275,000-square-foot industrial building in Buffalo, NY. The property, constructed in the early 2000s, is designed to accommodate both warehouse and manufacturing operations and was fully leased at the time of the loan closing.

data_points.notable_features: Can support both warehouse and manufacturing uses.

articles.title: Restoring An Industrial Core The Nonprofit Way: What Buffalo’s Northland Corridor Can Teach Other Cities
articles.narrative: This article argues that nonprofit-led redevelopment is a crucial strategy for revitalizing distressed industrial areas where traditional for-profit developers are hesitant to invest due to limited ROI potential. The author, an executive at Buffalo Urban Development Corp., highlights that nonprofits prioritize community outcomes, have access to diverse public funding, and can undertake complex, long-term projects like environmental remediation that for-profit entities often avoid. The Northland Corridor in Buffalo serves as a case study, demonstrating how a phased, mission-driven approach can create conditions for future private investment by focusing on workforce development and strategic site control, ultimately rebuilding economic drivers and fostering community trust.

articles.title: Constellation Breaks Ground on 492,624 SF Industrial Project in South Fort Worth
articles.narrative: Constellation Real Estate Partners has commenced construction on Constellation Summit 35, a substantial 492,624-square-foot industrial development in South Fort Worth. The project, situated on a 44-acre site, is designed with modern industrial specifications including 40-foot clear heights and ample parking for both cars and trailers. Completion is anticipated in the third quarter of next year, with KBC Advisors handling the leasing efforts.

data_points.notable_features: Features 40-foot clear heights and parking for 296 cars and 194 trailers.

articles.title: Partnership to Develop 90-Unit Affordable Seniors Housing Project in Houston
articles.narrative: A partnership between The NHP Foundation, Trinity East Village Community Development Corp., and Housing Alliance HTX is set to develop Trinity East Senior Village, a 90-unit affordable seniors housing project in Houston's Third Ward. Construction is slated to begin this summer, with an anticipated opening in 2027, addressing the need for age-restricted affordable housing in the area.

data_points.notable_features: Affordable seniors housing for residents age 55 and older.

articles.title: Housing Trust Group Completes 56-Unit Affordable Housing Conversion in Lubbock, Texas
articles.narrative: Housing Trust Group has completed the conversion of the historic Jim Kimmel Center in Lubbock, Texas, into a 56-unit affordable housing complex. The project involved transforming a vacant 1964-built motel and demolishing a former restaurant and gas station on the site. The units are designated for households earning 30% to 80% of the area median income.

data_points.notable_features: Historic conversion of a former 91-room motel.
data_points.project_notes: Units reserved for households earning 30-80% of area median income.

articles.title: Big tech still values the office, but in a different way
articles.narrative: A new report from Newmark indicates that major technology companies are reshaping their office footprints, focusing on fewer buildings, better locations, and higher-quality workplaces. The study, "Big Tech's U.S. Office Strategy Is Clear: Concentrate, Upgrade, Expand," reveals that the 100 largest office leases by U.S. tech occupiers over the past year totaled 16.5 million square feet across just 14 markets, with an average deal size of 165,000 square feet. This trend is largely driven by artificial intelligence firms and a desire to be near top talent and venture capital sources, particularly in the San Francisco Bay Area, New York City, and Boston. The report highlights that 83% of these leases were in top-tier properties, with most companies expanding their footprints rather than contracting, and lease terms are lengthening, signaling a continued commitment to physical office space as a strategic asset.

articles.title: Mid-America Real Estate Corporation brokers sale of 70,144-square-foot retail property in Park Ridge
articles.narrative: Mid-America Real Estate Corporation's Investment Sales Group recently brokered the sale of The Shops of Uptown, a 70,144-square-foot grocery-anchored retail property in Park Ridge, Illinois. The property, anchored by a popular grocery retailer, was sold by Phillips Edison Company to an institutional investment manager. The transaction highlights the strong demand for well-located retail assets in affluent suburban communities with robust demographics and consumer spending power.

articles.title: Prologis acquires 26 acres in Chicago’s Central DuPage submarket for 454,000-square-foot logistics development
articles.narrative: Prologis has acquired 26.19 acres in Glendale Heights, Illinois, for the development of two Class A speculative logistics facilities totaling 454,000 square feet. This acquisition represents the largest new industrial development ever planned for the land-constrained Central DuPage submarket, a historically strong industrial market in the Chicago area. The project aims to provide much-needed modern logistics space, featuring 36-foot clear heights and significant infrastructure improvements, supporting the region's supply chain.

data_points.address: 375 Army Trail Road, Glendale Heights, IL
data_points.notable_features: Two Class A logistics buildings with 36-foot clear heights and a shared 200-foot truck court, located in an established industrial corridor with direct access to Interstate 355.
data_points.project_notes: The acquisition includes 25.56 acres at 375 Army Trail Road and a 0.6-acre portion of 400 Regency Drive. The project will include a new connector road and upgrades to nearby intersections and stormwater management systems.

articles.title: Essex Realty Group closes sale of three multifamily properties in Chicago
articles.narrative: Essex Realty Group has facilitated the sale of three distinct multifamily properties across Chicago, totaling 20 units and approximately $9.6 million in transaction volume. The portfolio included a newly constructed luxury building in West Town, a value-add opportunity in Ukrainian Village, and a vacant repositioning asset in Uptown. These sales underscore sustained investor interest in diverse multifamily assets throughout the Chicago market, from luxury new builds to properties with significant upside potential.

data_points.project_notes: The properties included 1049 N. Wolcott Avenue (6 units, sold for $1,405,000), 918 W. Eastwood Avenue (6 units, sold for $1,985,000), and 1620 W. Grand Avenue (8 units, sold for $6,225,000).

articles.title: Marcus & Millichap brokers sale of retail strip in Schiller Park
articles.narrative: A six-suite retail strip property in Schiller Park, Illinois, was sold for $3.5 million to a local private investor. The buyer acquired the 23,000-square-foot center as part of a 1031 exchange, recognizing its potential despite short remaining lease terms. The property's conversion from a warehouse to a multi-tenant retail center and its proximity to Rosemont's convention and corporate presence were key attractions.

data_points.address: 4926 N. River Road, Schiller Park, IL
data_points.notable_features: Less than one mile from Interstate 294 and minutes from O’Hare International Airport, the Fashion Outlets of Chicago, and the Donald E. Stephens Convention Center. The property was converted from a former warehouse to a multi-tenant retail center.

articles.title: CREFC’s Aidasani: Capital is Back but is Selective (VIDEO)
articles.narrative: Raj Aidasani, managing director of research with the CRE Finance Council, notes that while capital is available in 2026, it is highly selective compared to the riskier lending environment of 2021. Lenders are now prioritizing strong underwriting assumptions, robust property fundamentals, and sponsor strength to ensure durable cash flows. Aidasani also clarified that while the Federal Reserve's actions influence the overnight Fed funds rate, the commercial real estate industry is more concerned with the longer end of the interest rate curve.

articles.title: Citi Lends $45M on Luxury East Village Multifamily
articles.narrative: JLL Capital Markets arranged $44.5 million in financing from Citi for Benchmark Real Estate Group's luxury multifamily property at 194 E. 2nd St. in Manhattan's East Village. The loan supports the 61-unit building, which also includes ground-floor retail. Benchmark Real Estate Group acquired the property in 2024 and completed extensive renovations to the residential units, common areas, lobby, and amenity spaces, positioning it as a high-quality asset in a market with strong demand and limited new supply.

articles.title: Andee Robb Joins Marcus & Millichap to Lead Retail Leasing & Advisory Services
articles.narrative: Andee Robb has been appointed as the head of Retail Leasing & Advisory Services at Marcus & Millichap, a newly created role aimed at expanding the firm's retail leasing business across North America. Robb, with over two decades of experience in retail real estate, will focus on identifying new opportunities, enhancing retailer engagement, and evolving the company's leasing platform. This strategic hire is part of Marcus & Millichap's broader initiative to strengthen its retail leadership, following the recent appointments of Michael Puline as senior managing director and national director of retail, and Thomas Gorman as senior managing director and national net lease division leader.

The transaction follows Alexander's recent sale of an adjacent property and a $175 million refinancing of the shopping center.

articles.title: Tapas Concept Fat of the Land Joining Restaurant Collection at Centerview Office Complex
articles.narrative: EMMES Realty Services and Oaktree Capital Management are expanding the dining options at their Centerview office complex in Irvine, CA, with the addition of Fat of the Land, a tapas restaurant. This new ground-floor establishment aims to enhance the hospitality-focused environment, serving both office tenants and the broader community. The addition is part of a strategy to create a vibrant sense of place through diverse dining experiences.

articles.title: The Housing Bill Sitting On Trump's Desk Isn't The Game-Changer Many Hoped — Or Feared
articles.narrative: The 21st Century Road to Housing Act, currently awaiting presidential signature, is considered a significant housing policy, though experts believe it will not be a game-changer for the commercial real estate sector. While it includes provisions to streamline environmental reviews, offer grants for increased housing supply, and remove the permanent chassis mandate for manufactured housing to reduce costs, its impact on the broader multifamily market is expected to be limited. The bill also raises the public welfare investment cap for banks and reauthorizes HUD's HOME Program, which are seen as positive signals for affordable housing development. However, some industry leaders view these measures as incremental rather than transformative, with one CEO noting they are more of a "tangent" for multifamily clients. The legislation also includes a cap on institutional ownership of single-family homes, though experts suggest there are exemptions and workarounds, particularly for new build-to-rent construction.

articles.title: Industrial Overtakes Multifamily In JLL Income Property Trust's Portfolio
articles.narrative: JLL Income Property Trust's portfolio now allocates 38% to industrial assets, totaling $2.8 billion, surpassing its residential holdings of 36% or $2.3 billion. The REIT's CEO, Allan Swaringen, noted that industrial properties offer higher cash-on-cash returns compared to apartments in the current market, making them a more attractive investment. The firm is strategically targeting last-mile logistics facilities near key transportation hubs, which allows for higher rent potential and tenant attraction. This shift is also influenced by macroeconomic factors such as increased U.S. manufacturing and defense spending, as well as companies building inventory due to global tensions and climate concerns.
articles.market_intelligence: Industrial leasing activity saw 174 million square feet of new leases in Q1 2026, marking the best Q1 performance since 2022. Concurrently, only 54 million square feet of new industrial projects came online. This absorption, coupled with reduced construction, has led to a 5.2% increase in industrial rents over the last year, with average rents reaching $9.12 per square foot as of May.

articles.title: D.C. Reveals Vision For RFK Campus With Up To 6,500 Homes
articles.narrative: The District of Columbia has unveiled its draft master plan for the 180-acre RFK Campus, envisioning a large-scale mixed-use development anchored by a new 70,000-seat stadium for the Washington Commanders. The plan, developed after extensive community feedback, proposes between 5,000 and 6,500 residential units, with 30% designated as affordable, alongside retail, hotel, and recreational spaces across six distinct districts. The D.C. Office of Planning aims to finalize the plan by year-end, with developer solicitations expected in late 2027 or early 2028, marking a significant step towards transforming the Anacostia Riverfront site into a 365-day community hub.

data_points.notable_features: Master plan for a 180-acre campus along the Anacostia River, anchored by a 70,000-seat football stadium, with 30% of residential units designated as affordable.
data_points.project_notes: The Washington Commanders are contributing $2.7B for the stadium, and D.C. has allocated $1.1B for infrastructure and a sports complex. The site was transferred from the federal government to the District with a mandate to preserve 30% for parks and open spaces. The plan includes 92,000 SF of retail in the Riverfront District and 150,000 SF of retail in the Plaza District.

articles.title: Horvath & Tremblay Expands Into Philly Market With Boutique Brokerage Acquisition
articles.narrative: Horvath & Tremblay, a Massachusetts-based brokerage, has acquired Scope Commercial Real Estate, a Philadelphia-based firm specializing in multifamily, retail, industrial, and office properties. This acquisition marks Horvath & Tremblay's significant entry into the Philadelphia market, leveraging Scope's established local relationships and expanding its regional presence. All 20 of Scope's employees will join Horvath & Tremblay, and Scope's office will become the new regional headquarters.

articles.title: Digital Realty Pays Blackstone $3.5B For Stake In 3 Virginia Data Centers
articles.narrative: Digital Realty is acquiring Blackstone's majority stake in three Northern Virginia data centers for $3.5 billion in a cash-and-stock deal. The transaction involves Digital Realty taking full ownership of two 96 MW data centers in Manassas and a 96 MW data center in Sterling, which were developed through a 2023 joint venture between the two firms. The facilities are fully leased to investment-grade tenants, with two expected to be fully operational in early 2027 and the third in 2028. This acquisition allows Digital Realty to increase its ownership in high-quality hyperscale assets and expand its strategic private capital platform.

data_points.notable_features: Three data centers totaling 288 MW of capacity, fully leased to investment-grade tenants.
data_points.project_notes: The three data centers have a combined value of $7.8 billion, including debt and planned capital expenditures. Payment to Blackstone includes $1.2 billion in cash and $2.3 billion in Digital Realty stock. This transaction follows a 2023 joint venture between Digital Realty and Blackstone to develop hyperscale data centers in Virginia, France, and Germany, a $7 billion partnership where Blackstone held majority stakes and Digital Realty handled construction and operations.
